title: Marketplace transaction flow copy + ops preflight (draft)
content:
Purpose
This working doc pulls together suggested listing copy focused specifically on purchase/entitlement/transaction messaging and a parallel operations preflight checklist for cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). Goal: produce ready-to-drop copy blocks and a concise ops checklist so engineering + finance + legal can sign off quickly. NOT the final microsite — this is the transactional surface and prelaunch operational runbook.

What’s in scope (this doc)
- Short product blurb and three CTA/checkout copy variants (trial-first, immediate-purchase, self-serve seat plan)
- SKU naming and meter descriptors by marketplace model (usage v. subscription)
- Technical ops preflight checklist (billing hooks, entitlement mapping, onboarding flow, telemetry to monitor)
- Known open questions and owners

Audience
Primary: marketplace listing owner (GTM/Product), billing/integration engineer, finance (billing reconciliation), sales/solutions (contract edge cases).

COPY — short form (for listing tile / pricing tile / checkout)
Variant A — Trial-first (recommended for PLG motion)
Title: Try Redwood Inference (Free 14‑day Trial)
One-liner: High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost — spin up a trial and test at your scale.
CTA: Start free trial — no credit card required
Checkout microcopy: You’ll get 14 days of Dedicated trial credits (equivalent to X GPU hours). After trial end you can convert to subscription or continue on usage-based billing.

Variant B — Immediate subscription (SaaS buyers / procurement)
Title: Redwood Inference — Dedicated & Hosted API
One-liner: Production-grade LLM inference: SLA-backed dedicated capacity, private deployment options, and per-token pricing tailored for production traffic.
CTA: Purchase subscription
Checkout microcopy: Choose a monthly commitment. Billing will run through the marketplace; Redwood will provision capacity once purchase completes. Contact sales to set up private deployment.

Variant C — Consumption-first (developer self-serve)
Title: Pay-as-you-go LLM inference (hosted API)
One-liner: Start with usage-based pricing — no capacity commitments, predictable per-token unit pricing, fast onboarding.
CTA: Get API keys and start calling
Checkout microcopy: After purchase you’ll receive a marketplace entitlement and a Redwood API key. Map entitlement to Redwood account during onboarding (see onboarding steps).

SKU and Meter Descriptor Suggestions
(These strings should be readable in marketplace UI and map to our internal billing product codes)
- sku.redwood.inference.hosted.tokens – "Host Token Units (per 1k tokens)" – unit pricing, meters by 1k token blocks.
- sku.redwood.inference.dedicated.month – "Dedicated Capacity (monthly commitment)" – monthly seat/pool SKU.
- sku.redwood.inference.private.license – "Private Deployment License (annual)" – license fee for private control plane.
- sku.redwood.inference.support.premium – "Enterprise Support Add-on (SLA+AES)" – per-seat or flat add-on.
- sku.redwood.inference.trial.credit – "Trial Credits (one-time)" – provisioning event to grant trial quota.

Marketplace-specific copy notes
- AWS: call out IAM role mapping and marketplace entitlement sync latency. Use the phrase "Marketplace entitlement provisioning may take up to 10 minutes" in checkout microcopy.
- Azure: mention subscription mapping to Azure AD tenant. Include a note about AAD admin consent for connector.
- GCP: reference project-level IAM binding and service account key exchange step.

Onboarding step microcopy (to include on post-purchase landing)
1) Verify entitlement (we’ll pull your marketplace entitlement automatically; if it doesn’t appear, click ‘Link account’.)
2) Create or connect Redwood account (SSO / email)
3) Map entitlement to Redwood project (select project -> apply entitlement)
4) Provision resources (if Dedicated: choose region and capacity; if Hosted: API keys created)
5) Confirm billing and support contact

Operational preflight checklist (engineering + finance + legal)
- Billing & Entitlement
  - [ ] SKU names created in marketplace catalog and mapped to internal product codes (owner: Miguel Ortega)
  - [ ] Entitlement webhook endpoint implemented and tested (dev endpoint + staging + prod) — ensure idempotency for duplicate notifications (owner: Ethan Park)
  - [ ] Trial credit provisioning flow implemented (one-off grant) and tested to expire correctly (owner: Priya Nair)
  - [ ] Reconciliation pipeline for marketplace invoices in finance system (owner: Leah Morgan)
- Authentication & Account Mapping
  - [ ] OAuth/SSO flows documented per marketplace (AWS IAM, Azure AD, GCP IAM) and smoke tested (owner: Miguel Ortega)
  - [ ] Entitlement-to-account mapping UX validated (edge case: multiple marketplace entitlements across multiple Redwood accounts) (owner: Priya Nair)
- Provisioning & Capacity
  - [ ] Dedicated provisioning automation: region selection, pool size, and autoscale policy validation (owner: Platform Eng runbook)
  - [ ] Graceful fallback policy defined: when Dedicated unavailable, route to Hosted variant and tag request (owner: Serving Runtime)
- Observability & Telemetry
  - [ ] Event emitted for purchase, entitlement link, provisioning start/complete, and first API call — wire to internal MP Launch dashboard (owner: Observability)
  - [ ] Billing meter accurate to within acceptable variance (±2%) vs. internal token counters (owner: Finance)
  - [ ] Alert: entitlement webhook failures > 5 in 30m (owner: SRE)
- Legal & Commercial
  - [ ] Marketplace contract language checked vs Redwood standard terms (owner: Legal)
  - [ ] Data residency and data-processing addendum referenced for private deployments (owner: Security & Compliance)
  - [ ] Support SLA escalation path documented and included in listing copy where required (owner: Customer Success)
- Assets & UX
  - [ ] Logo (PNG + SVG), 1200x628 hero, icon 128px, and 72px thumbnails uploaded (owner: Design)
  - [ ] Short description (≤ 250 chars), full description (≤ 1500 chars), and feature bullets prepared (owner: Product)
  - [ ] One short demo video (45–90s) hosted and linked (owner: Developer Experience)
- Pricing & Accounting
  - [ ] Marketplace unit economics validated (expected margin delta, fees) and passed to pricing committee (owner: Finance)
  - [ ] Billing SKUs listed with exact unit and rounding rules (owner: Finance)

Launch timeline (example)
- D-21: Finalize SKU names and entitlement endpoints (engineering + finance sign-off)
- D-14: Upload assets, copy into marketplace console, legal approval starts
- D-7: End-to-end smoke test (purchase -> entitlement -> provisioning -> first API call)
- D-3: Final QA pass, marketing prep for microsite traffic
- D0: Go live

Edge cases & unresolved questions (short list)
- What is the exact conversion mapping between marketplace token meter and internal token counters for multi-model responses (owner: Serving Runtime, due: 2025-11-18). Need a mapping doc + test harness.
- For AWS consolidated billing customers purchasing multiple SKUs across accounts, how do we dedupe and link a single Redwood project? (owner: Billing Integration; blocker until D-14)
- Should trial credit be a separate SKU or a one-time grant via the entitlement API? (ops preference: grant; marketplace preference: SKU). Decision owner: Priya Nair.

Sample longer description (for listing page) — first draft
"Redwood Inference delivers production-grade LLM serving with predictable latency and clear unit economics. Choose hosted API for fastest time-to-value, reserve Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, or deploy in your VPC for regulated workloads. This listing authorizes provisioning and billing through the marketplace. After purchase we’ll link your entitlement to your Redwood account and either provide API keys or deploy dedicated capacity in your selected region. 14-day trials are available for evaluation."

Quick QA checklist for copy reviewers
- [ ] Does the short description mention deployment modes?
- [ ] Is trial language consistent with other GTM channels?
- [ ] Are support contact and SLA summary present and accurate?
- [ ] Do asset filenames and variants match the marketplace upload form requirements?

Communication playbook for purchase events (ops runbook snippet)
- On purchase: send a confirmation email (template A) and create a ticket in support queue labeled "Marketplace Purchase".
- On provisioning complete: send provisioning email and link to onboarding doc; run an automated smoke call and emit metric purchase.provisioning.success.
- Failure modes: if provisioning fails twice, escalate to oncall engineering and send buyer an apology + ETA + option for refund.

Notes-to-self and leftovers
- Need final pricing table with example bills for 10M tokens/month, 100M tokens/month, and dedicated 8-GPU pool for a 30-day month. (Finance)
- Confirm whether marketplace requires a separate EULA acceptance screen for private deployment license. (Legal)
- Record all smoke test runs with timestamps and GitHub Actions artifacts for audit. (SRE)

Owners/Points of Contact
- Product & Copy: Ava Chen
- Billing integration: Miguel Ortega
- Engineering (entitlements + webhooks): Ethan Park
- Finance reconciliation: Leah Morgan
- Legal review: Nora Patel (cc’ed via Confluence)

Next steps
- Miguel to create SKUs in test marketplace and share IDs (due: 2026-01-10)
- Ethan to post webhook test harness and sample payloads to linked_artifacts above (due: 2026-01-17)
- Priya to decide trial SKU vs entitlement grant (due: 2026-01-14)

End of draft.

(Version: mp-trxflow-v0.1)
